chunks: From him, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Ash'ath ibn Muhammad al-Bariqi, from Abdul Karim ibn Salih who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and saw three green pigeons on his mattress, which had defecated on it. I said, 'May I be your ransom, these pigeons have dirtied the mattress.' He said, 'No, it is recommended that they dwell in the house.'

key_terms.تُسْكَنَ: to be dwelled in / to reside

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to keep pigeons inside the house according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the presence of pigeons and their droppings on the bed is not considered impurity (najasah) or dirtiness in a way that detracts from the home's sanctity, but rather a sign of domestic tranquility. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that keeping birds indoors is a recommended practice (mustahabb) for companionship and peace, prioritizing the spiritual and emotional comfort derived from their presence over rigid aesthetic cleanliness. The hadith underscores the Ahl al-Bayt's practical approach to household management, where minor mess is tolerated for greater benefit.
